Vendored on:       2026-08-28T00:00:00Z (A1.1 productionization, issue #49)
RE-PINNED on:      2026-08-28 (A2.0 issue #101 — in-repo substrate rework:
                    ms_ctx_t v2 168B -> v3 176B, resume-table/global removal)

FILES (same basenames as the SPIKE spike/colorless_runtime/vendor/
mojito-sys/ tree; the spike harness links this same dylib, built from
PROD only). NOT asserted byte-identical with SPIKE: this file used to
claim `diff -r` between the two vendored dirs was empty, which had been
false since #101 landed here without a matching re-vendor of SPIKE
(issue #170 instance 6). See mojito_async/vendor/check-vendored.sh
finding [4] and VENDORED_EXCEPTIONS.tsv's `spike:` rows for exactly which
files diverge and why:
  include/mojito_spike.h   # ms_ctx_t v3 layout (176 B: x19-x30, d8-d15, sp,
                           #   return_to @168)
  native_stack.c           # ms_stack_alloc/free with PROT_NONE guard page
  aarch64_switch.S         # ms_ctx_make/ms_ctx_switch (Apple arm64; #if
                           #   !__APPLE__ guard)
  ms_ctx.c                 # compile-time layout asserts + sentinel probe
                           #   (guarded off)

DEVIATION FROM FROZEN (issue #101, A2.0 M:N rework) — RECORDED:
  The frozen S0 substrate was single-OS-thread-only and capped at 32 live
  fibers: `_ms_ctx_switch` kept a process-global 64-row `_ms_resume_tab`
  (2 rows/fiber, never evicted -> brk #0x67 on exhaustion) and updated
  `_ms_last_from`/`_ms_last_to` on every switch; the exit trampoline read
  `_ms_last_to` to learn its own ctx (clobbered the moment a 2nd OS thread
  switched).  This a2/00 re-pin REMOVES those globals and the O(64) scan:
  the return link now rides INSIDE the context as ms_ctx_t.return_to (O(1)),
  and the trampoline derives its own ctx from a marker ms_ctx_make stashes
  at [stack_top-8] on the fiber's own stack (no shared writable state on the
  switch path) => thread-safe for M:N, no live-fiber cap.  Layout grows
  168 B -> 176 B; every consumer uses MS_CTX_SIZE (mojito_async vendor
  firewall, spike mojito_spike.mojo), so block offsets follow automatically.
  Verified by the A1 suite (t23/t25/t26/t16 exact-switch proofs intact),
  t27_concurrency (40 live fibers, was capped), t27_multithread (two-pthread
  probe, was clobbered), and the spike harness.

The #101 rework itself landed identically in both the prod and spike
vendored copies; they have since diverged elsewhere (issue #170 instance
6 — see the FILES note above, not a re-litigation of #101). See the
aarch64_switch.S header comment for the full ISSUE #101 rationale, and
precommit/known-red.tsv for the RED->GREEN evidence.
